structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E040.

**Tip (E036, unchanged).** 231 steps at batch 2000; 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%; whitening detached from 20% of steps; stem frozen at 75%. Measured 5.314 s and 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Seeds 13–22 gave 0.7525 (E038), so the population mean is about 0.7528. That is zero margin against the 0.753 local bar and about 0.25 pp against the official bar.

**E040.** 40/0/30/30 saved 0.117 s (2.2%), which I forecast correctly at 5.20. It measured 0.7526 (−0.06 pp, within noise) but missed the 0.753 bar. The 20-vs-24 px split is cheap but not free, and with zero margin even about 0.05 pp sinks a keep.

**Time model.** Time ≈ F (about 0.25 s) + Σ steps × per-step cost. Hits in 11 of the last 12 runs.
- Per step: about 0.032 s at 32 px, 0.026 at 28, 0.021 at 24, 0.016 at 20.
- Discounts: whitening detach about −8%; freeze about −27% at 32 px.
- One full-to-truncated switch at 32 px saves about 0.0085 s. One 20 px step removed saves about 0.015 s.
- Bandwidth-bound savings arrive at or above face value (E028, E034, E036). Small-map BN is not a lever (E039: 0.6%).

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epochs: 1.5–2.5.
- Freeze at 75%: about 2.
- 20 px replacing 24 px: about 2 (E040, noisy).
- Whitening detach: ≥1.
- Freeze moved to 60%: about 0.65.
- Width cut: about 0.7.
- BN fold: about 0.15.

At zero margin, any lever saving about 0.1 s needs an accuracy funder of about 0.1 pp. Steps are the only proven funder.

**Accuracy boosters.** All four schedule and regularization tweaks were ≤0 on held-out seeds (E025, E029, E030, E032). Prior for untested ones: −0.15 ± 0.25 pp.

BN recalibration after training leaves the trajectory unchanged, so its effect is a paired, low-noise delta. My prior is +0.05 ± 0.15 pp. With BN momentum 0.6, the running stats are dominated by the last few batches, then lerped by Lookahead, so recalibration might help slightly.

**Mechanisms:**
1. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is already tuned.
2. Accuracy is built at 28/32 px and needs a trainable stem until about 70–75% of steps (E011, E018, E024, E033, E037). The early phase is cheap but each trim costs about 0.05–0.1 pp.
3. Large-map backward is bandwidth-bound.
4. Any trajectory change re-draws the RNG and moves the 3-seed mean by ±0.1–0.3 pp.

**Noise:**
- Per-seed std about 0.3 pp; 3-seed SE about 0.17 pp; 10-seed SE about 0.1 pp.
- Time noise about 1% (0.05 s).

**Unsure:**
- Whether the PCIe judge discounts bandwidth-bound savings.
- Whether 16 px (1×1 final map) breaks early features.
- Where the freeze cliff sits between 60% and 75% (pre- or post-32 px switch).
- Muon's unconfounded value.

forecasts.reason: No recipe change. A profiler trace will likely show the 31x31 BN/GELU/pool work and group 1 well above their MAC share, as E028/E036 savings imply.
12 steps at 20 px x 0.015 s saves about 0.18 s. The schedule stretch plus fewer steps costs about 0.1 pp, close to the 0.1 pp bound.
About 35 steps (60-75%) without conv1 wgrad or 31x31 backward saves about 0.1 s. A milder version of E037's cliff likely costs 0.1-0.2 pp.
12 more truncated 32 px steps x 0.0085 s saves about 0.1 s. Accuracy cost about 0.1 pp (between 75% at 0 and 60% at -0.4), which misses the bar at zero margin.
3 forward-only 32 px batches plus augmentation cost about 0.04 s. A paired gain of about +0.05 pp is likely below the 0.15 pp keep threshold.
About 35 steps at 16 vs 20 px saves about 0.16 s. A 1x1 final map early likely costs 0.1-0.3 pp.
Math-identical. A 0.07 s trial-0 cut is about 0.02 s on the mean, below the 0.05 s time noise.

cruxes: Does any time-neutral change (BN recalibration I064, or something else) raise held-out accuracy by at least 0.15 pp? Without one, every 0.1 s lever fails the zero-margin bar.
Is the freeze cliff tied to the 28→32 px switch (I063 near-neutral at 70%) or a smooth dose response (about -0.1 pp per 5% of steps)?
Should the loop instead buy margin with steps (+0.25 epoch ≈ +0.15 s) and then stack several cheap trims (20 px trim, 16 px start, 70% freeze) whose combined exchange rate beats the epoch dial?
